title: Lily  Wu
text: Lily  Wu - Lily Wu Mayor City of Wichita Class of '07 | Wichita, KS Personal Website Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Instagram Overview Mayor Lily Wu was elected Mayor of Wichita on November 7, 2023, and was sworn in as the City of Wichita’s 103rd mayor on January 8, 2024. Mayor Lily is the first woman elected to a full term in the largest city in Kansas. She is the first Asian American mayor in the state of Kansas. Mayor Lily speaks Cantonese and Spanish, was born in Guatemala, and immigrated to Wichita, Kansas with her family in 1993. On her 30th anniversary of coming to America, she announced her candidacy for mayor. She champions an inclusive vision for the entire city focused on ensuring public safety, strengthening our economy, restoring trust in City Hall and building a united community. Prior to being elected, Mayor Lily spent 12 years as a journalist, serving as an anchor and reporter for Wichita television stations KAKE and KWCH 12 News. Mayor Lily is dedicated to serving the community as an active community volunteer for various organizations. She is a member of the Citizen Police Academy Alumni Association, Civic Engagement Academy Alumni, Steve Clark YMCA Advisory Board, WSU Barton School of Business Dean’s Alumni Council, Wichita Crime Commission, and Wichita Asian Association. Mayor Lily previously served on the boards of Botanica’s Chinese Garden of Friendship, Diversity Kansas, Orpheum Theatre, Students In Free Enterprise, Visioneering Wichita, and WSU Alumni Association. Mayor Lily graduated from the International Baccalaureate program at Wichita East High School. As a Gore Scholar at Wichita State University, she graduated Summa Cum Laude with two bachelor’s degrees in international business and integrated marketing communication. While serving as a Rotary Ambassadorial Scholar, she also earned a master’s degree in journalism from the University of Hong Kong. She received the “2024 Spotlight Award” by the Asian Pacific American Institute for Congressional Studies (APAICS) Women’s Collective in Seattle on June 28. Lily was named the “2022 Rising Star in TV” by the Kansas Association of Broadcasters, “2020 Exceptional Young Leader” by the Wichita Regional Chamber of Commerce, and a “2015 Leader in Diversity” by the Wichita Business Journal. In 2012, she was crowned Miss Kansas United States. Mayor Lily enjoys spending time with her family, friends and Samoyed dog daughter Aspen.

This award gives me assurance that the career I am pursuing is what I am meant to do and that I made the right decision. Though the road has not always been smooth, winning this award made me realize that my efforts were worthwhile. I would tell others that it is okay to be scared and unsure about your career or major choice. Feeling a little lost is completely normal. College is an opportunity not only to discover your career path but also to learn more about yourself. Your grades don't define your intelligence or your self worth. If you struggle with an assignment or a test, do not be too hard on yourself. College is a roller coaster of emotions and events, but just remember to be yourself. Stay true to yourself regardless of what others say. My biggest mentor has been one of my accounting professors, Professor Michael Flores. He helped me prepare for the interview for the semi-finalist round. He has inspired me to become a better student and a better person overall. Frank Barton School Of Business Class of 2025 Overview David Eby Major: Finance Expected Graduation: Fall 2025 Hometown: Overland Park, Kansas David Eby is a finance major and graduate student in business analytics whose path is defined by focus and follow-through. He chose Wichita State University for its innovation and for the Barton School’s real-world connections with employers throughout the region. On campus, David serves as President of Delta Upsilon Fraternity and is a member of the Cummings Student Managed Investment Fund. He enjoys working on projects that turn theoretical learning into practical solutions. One of his most rewarding experiences was a final project for Intro to Business Analytics, where his team presented data-driven findings to Textron Defense. That experience affirmed his belief in how classroom learning directly applies to industry problems. After earning his master’s degree, David plans to gain experience in finance and analytics before taking a leadership role in his family business. He aspires to combine data insight with entrepreneurial vision to drive growth and innovation. Outside of academics, David enjoys the outdoors and is an avid hiker and hammock camper. He finds balance and perspective in nature, which reminds him to stay grounded amid his busy schedule. He credits his father as his greatest influence as both a mentor and voice of reason. A trusted guide for David throughout all of life’s decisions, his father remains a constant source of support. Being recognized as one of Barton’s 25 Under 25 is a meaningful milestone for David. It reflects his dedication to leadership, his belief in lifelong learning, and his desire to build a career that balances data with heart.

Immersed in another culture, Rene gained a deeper appreciation for history, art, and storytelling, which ignited his dream of becoming a film director someday. He hopes to combine his financial expertise and creative vision to build businesses that connect culture and technology. Rene’s greatest inspiration comes from his family, especially his parents, whose perseverance and faith taught him that success is about lifting others along the way. He honors their legacy by working to create opportunities for his younger brothers and his community. Outside his academic life, Rene collects analog watches. These traditional mechanical treasures remind him to value craftsmanship and time itself. Being recognized as one of Barton’s 25 Under 25 is an achievement that fills Rene with gratitude. It marks a journey of hard work, faith, and family, and a commitment to creating a future defined by hope and impact.

text: Trent J. Deines - Trent J. Deines Business Administration Major W. Frank Barton School Of Business Class of 2027 Overview Trent J. He chose the Barton School of Business after seeing firsthand the university’s investment in student success and the welcoming environment created by faculty and staff. The experience convinced him that Wichita State was the right place to grow academically and professionally. For Trent, meaningful growth has come through applying what he learns in the classroom to real-world experiences. title: Cohen  Ayres
text: Cohen  Ayres - Cohen Ayres International Business, Entrepreneurship and Marketing Majors W. Frank Barton School Of Business Class of 2026 Overview Cohen Ayres Majors: International Business, Entrepreneurship and Marketing Expected Graduation: Spring 2026 Hometown: Garden Plain, Kansas Cohen Ayres is an international business, entrepreneurship and marketing major who brings leadership, curiosity, and dedication to every space he enters. Raised a proud Shocker by two WSU alumni, Cohen grew up connected to Wichita State and always envisioned himself studying at the Barton School of Business. Cohen has been a two-term Chapter President of Sigma Phi Epsilon and also served as Vice President of the SigEp Learning Community. Leading the organization through cultural transformation, academic improvement, and national recognition has been the most meaningful achievement of his time at WSU. These accomplishments were made possible by the Rudd Scholar Program and several additional scholarships that made his education and leadership involvement accessible. A standout leader, Cohen plans to work for Sigma Phi Epsilon Headquarters after graduation, traveling to support chapters nationwide or managing a regional portfolio. Later, he hopes to earn an MBA and pursue a career in strategy and management consulting. Cohen is inspired by his father, one of the earliest recipients of the Jabara Scholarship, who proved that education can be made attainable through dedication and opportunity. Following in those footsteps as a second-generation Jabara Scholar is something Cohen carries with pride. Something many people do not know about Cohen is that he grew up on a farm, running his own small chicken and duck operations and helping with his family’s Wagyu business, Wheat State Wagyu. Those early experiences taught him the value of hard work and sparked his interest in entrepreneurship. Cohen’s decision to add marketing to his major came after a professor shifted his perspective by saying, “everything is marketing.” That idea transformed the way he views business and shaped his approach to problem-solving. Being recognized as one of Barton’s 25 Under 25 is a profound honor for Cohen. It acknowledges his effort and the dedication he brings to every commitment, while motivating him to continue making an impact that reflects the values of leadership, service, and integrity.

title: Cat  Powner
text: Cat  Powner - Cat Powner Accounting Major W. Frank Barton School Of Business Class of 2025 Overview Cat Powner Major: Accounting Expected Graduation: Fall 2025 Hometown: Wichita, Kansas Cat Powner is an accounting major whose journey at the Barton School of Business reflects determination, growth, and gratitude. She chose Wichita State University for its strong job placement record, supportive faculty, and the unmatched opportunities that Woolsey Hall provides. The Barton School’s culture encouraged her to seek out new challenges, build meaningful relationships, and pursue excellence both inside and outside the classroom. Cat has been involved in Beta Alpha Psi and The National Society of Leadership and Success, organizations that have shaped her leadership skills and strengthened her professional focus. However, one of the most influential moments in her college journey occurred at the very first business job fair she attended. Unsure of what to expect, Cat walked in hoping simply to gain insight. Instead, she secured two job offers. One of those roles became the position she has held for more than a year, and she recently accepted a full-time offer with that same company. That experience became a defining moment, showing her that Barton students are highly sought after and that her hard work had real value. Cat has been inspired by the exceptional mentors she met at Textron Aviation. They encouraged her to perform at her best while also reminding her that academics are a priority. Her managers modeled professionalism, compassion, and balance, helping her learn what it means to be both a strong employee and a committed student. Her passion for accounting stems from a love of math and problem-solving. She appreciates that accounting offers clarity, structure, and purpose, and she enjoys the challenge of interpreting information that helps organizations operate effectively. Cat also values the stability and long-term potential of the field, viewing it as a profession that will always be essential. A fun fact about Cat is that she holds dual citizenship in Canada and the United States. Her multicultural background contributes to her adaptability and openness to new experiences. Being named one of Barton’s 25 Under 25 represents the hard work, commitment, and growth Cat has demonstrated throughout her college journey. She is proud to represent the Barton School and looks forward to building a future grounded in purpose, skill, and passion.

title: Steve Wilson
text: Steve Wilson - Steve Wilson Project Manager Ennovar – Textron Aviation Overview Steve Wilson is a seasoned Cybersecurity Analyst with over 20 years of experience in the IT industry, including 15 years as an IT Technician and 7 years specializing in cybersecurity. Steve plays a critical role in safeguarding organizational assets and ensuring compliance with industry standards. His responsibilities include overseeing software security, ensuring applications are protected against vulnerabilities, and maintaining secure development practices across the organization. One of his key accomplishments includes implementing an application whitelist encompassing over 10,000 applications, significantly enhancing endpoint security and reducing attack surface across the enterprise. With a keen eye for vulnerabilities and a proactive approach to incident response, he contributes to building resilient security infrastructures that protect against evolving cyber threats. Outside of work, Steve enjoys spending quality time with his family and unwinding on the golf course, balancing his professional drive with personal fulfillment.

Schlapp uses his leadership skills in developing strategies to fulfill the University’s mission statement, implementing initiatives across university divisions, collaboratively working with community leaders, businesses and stakeholders for the betterment of the region. In 2020 he was promoted to his current position as the Executive Director of Government Relations & Strategy, he also serves as Director of NIAR Business Development, Executive Director of the WSU Board of Trustees and Wichita State Innovation Alliance and Operations. Schlapp graduated from Kansas State University with a bachelor's in business administration and received a master's in public administration from Wichita State University. Mr. Schlapp is currently a member of the Governor's military council and on the executive board of the Sedgwick County developmental disability organization. Andy and his wife, Jane, have three children. title: Sierra  Bonn
text: Sierra  Bonn - Sierra Bonn Student Speaker Overview Sierra Marie Bonn has been passionate about making the world a better place since she joined Girl Scouts as a young girl. She recently graduated from Wichita State with a Bachelor’s in Engineering Technology with a focus in Management and a minor in Anthropology. During college, Sierra was named a Stanford University Innovation Fellow, served as part of the Presidential Search Committee tasked with searching for WSU’s 15th President, and currently serves the state of Kansas as Miss Southwest 2020-21. Sierra is the founder of “Let’s Go Full STEAM Ahead!” a nonprofit dedicated to STEAM (science, technology, engineering, arts, and math) education and engagement to empower the next generation of innovators. Through her podcast and sales of her children’s book, “Innovators: women in history who have made positive contributions to STEAM,” Sierra has created a scholarship foundation to help young women pursue innovative careers.

title: Chris  Cavanaugh
text: Chris  Cavanaugh - Chris Cavanaugh Director of Internal Audit Services (316) 978-5823 chris.cavanaugh@wichita.edu High-Resolution Photo Overview Chris Cavanaugh is the Director of Internal Audit Services at WSU, providing internal audit services to the university president, vice presidents, deans, directors, department chairs, and others. He has worked in this position since 1991 under six presidents, including our current president, Dr. Rick Muma. According to Cavanaugh, internal auditing involves both assurance and advisory components. Is information reliable, are processes working effectively, and are compliance requirements satisfied? If not, how can we work together to improve internal control ? Cavanaugh holds bachelor's and master's degrees in accounting from Pittsburg State University, and he is a Certified Public Accountant (CPA) and a Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE). His extensive knowledge and experience in risk assessment and control processes led him to establish the WSU Internal Control All-Star digital credential to create awareness about the critical importance of establishing an ethical culture and effective systems of internal control. Before joining WSU, Cavanaugh worked eight years as an internal auditor for the Farm Credit Bank of Wichita, where he advanced to Associate Vice President for Internal Audit. He also has public accounting experience and taught managerial accounting at Pittsburg State and Wichita State. Outside WSU, Cavanaugh serves on the Campus Credit Union board of directors as its treasurer and as a member of its Executive Committee. He previously chaired the credit union's Supervisory Committee. Chris Cavanaugh grew up in the west Wichita suburb of Goddard, where he listened to Shockers football and basketball games on the radio and went to games with his dad or friends whenever he could. After college, he returned to Goddard with his wife, Mary Kay, and raised four children there. The couple enjoy long walks with their dog Bailey on the "rails to trails" path near their home, and Chris is a regular at the weekly Exploration Place Parkrun 5K .
